dataset.name: Mars Science Laboratory Radiation Assessment Detector
dataset.observationPeriod: Curiosity's first 10 months on the surface of Mars

observations.name: Average radiation measured by Curiosity
observations.description: During its first 10 months on Mars, NASA's Curiosity rover measured an average of about 210 microgray of absorbed radiation each day from galactic cosmic rays.
observations.educationalExplanation: Radiation is energy that travels through space. Curiosity measured about 210 microgray per day from galactic cosmic rays during its first 10 months on Mars. Microgray is a unit scientists use to describe absorbed radiation energy.

observedFeatures.name: Galactic cosmic rays
observedFeatures.description: They contributed almost all of the observed surface radiation during the reported period.

observedFeatures.name: Forbush decreases
observedFeatures.description: NASA reported sudden reductions in measured radiation associated with additional shielding from interplanetary coronal mass ejections.

observedFeatures.name: Solar particle events
observedFeatures.description: Only one weak solar particle event was observed by RAD on the surface during the reported period.

limitations: These are historical observations, not current live measurements.
The reported average is not a prediction of radiation exposure during the ARES-6 mission.
Absorbed dose in microgray is not the same as dose equivalent in microsievert.
The game's radiation risk points are fictional gameplay values and must not be treated as measured radiation doses.
